items.caption:
Cabo Girão by boat from Funchal, Madeira: six seconds of cliff, and two yellow dots.

The dots are buoys. Look just above the middle of the water, side by side, like two small eyes keeping watch on the beach.

Behind them: a strip of grey pebbles, then terraces with a few flat roofs and stone walls, then rock in red and green all the way up and out of the frame. The camera gave up before the cliff did.

Nobody built those terraces for the view. They got it anyway.

Duas boias, uma praia, e uma montanha por cima.

Both our trips come along here from the marina. The Day Trip stops at Fajã dos Padres for the swim and paddle, the Sunset Trip turns at Cabo Girão as the light goes. Your group only, five at most.

Six seconds is the Reel. The boat gives you a bit longer. Book direct on chifbay.com

items.caption:
Private boat trip out of Funchal, Madeira: the town is behind us and the glasses are still empty.

Two white glasses on the edge of the boat, a bottle in the bucket, and a trail of foam where we have just been.

Look at Funchal from here. The whole town sits on a slope, as if somebody tipped the island towards the sea and the houses slid down as far as the harbour wall.

The glasses are not glass, by the way. White plastic, so they look smarter than they are. Real glass and a wake like that do not get along.

Funchal a ficar pequeno, o mar a ficar grande.

Both our trips leave from Marina do Funchal and head this way, west along the coast. Day Trip with the swim stop at Fajã dos Padres, or Sunset Trip as the light goes, and food on board on either one.

We keep it to five people on board. Send us your dates and we will tell you what is free.

Wild dolphins alongside the boat. Respectful distance, never chasing.

Private boat from Funchal, skipper included, five guests maximum.

Book direct on chifbay.com

Food on board a private boat from Funchal, Madeira: the table is set and the sea is the tablecloth.

On our table: a bottle of passion fruit poncha, a bottle of Madeira wine, a bowl of olives, little cubes of cheese and slices of chouriço.

The poncha has the better label. A passion fruit cut open, in case you were unsure what is inside.

Behind the bottles, the Karnic seats are pale and clean, and past the rail the water is a very bright turquoise. It looks like it was added afterwards. It was not.

Mesa posta, mar à volta.

Food on board comes with every trip we run, the Day Trip and the Sunset Trip alike. Just your group, five at most, and a skipper who also knows where the bottle opener lives.

Olives first or cheese first? Book direct on chifbay.com

Swimming in Madeira, seen from straight above: one person, one rock pool, and the Atlantic kept outside.

Look for the small pale shape floating in the dark blue water, left of centre. That is a swimmer, and they have the whole pool to themselves.

On the right, the waves are throwing white foam at the rocks. On the left, the water inside is calm and clear enough to see the stones on the bottom. One strip of rock is all that separates the two.

There are even a few stone steps in the top left corner, in case the pool wants you to feel invited.

Swimming is part of our Day Trip only, from Funchal marina, with a swim and paddle stop at Fajã dos Padres. The Sunset Trip is for the light, not for the water. Both are private, five guests at most.

Água calma de um lado, mar bravo do outro.

Would you swim in the calm side, or just watch the waves?

Madeira swim stop from above: a floating swimmer, a crooked stone wall and the whole Atlantic trying to get in.

The swimmer is on their back, in red, arms out, right of centre. Not a care in the picture.

The wall is the clever part. It bends at an angle like a folded ruler, and behind it the water turns green and clear. On the other side of the rock, the sea is all white foam and dark blue.

Some good planning went into that wall. Or some very patient waves.

The practical bit: swimming is on our Day Trip only. It leaves Funchal marina at 10:00 or 14:00, takes 2h30 or 3h, and stops at Fajã dos Padres for a swim and paddle. The Sunset Trip has no swimming. Both are private, five guests at most, with food on board.

Bring a towel. We will bring the rest.

Dia de mar, sem pressa.
